findings.title: Python factory model is incompatible with repository factory-as-code schema
findings.requirement: The CLI must load and execute the factories declared in .agent-os/factories.
findings.reproduction: uv run agent-os factory-validate .agent-os/factories/build.yaml exits 1 with Pydantic errors because Python expects name/version/runner/capabilities while the repository schema defines id/roles/phases/transitions/artifacts/tools/budgets/gates/escalation/retry/cleanup.
findings.impact: The advertised factory selection and factory-aware demo do not work with any shipped factory.
findings.recommendation: Use one canonical factory model/schema, generate or cross-validate it, and add a parametrized test that loads every registered enabled factory through both validators and runs demo for each.
findings.verification: All registry entries load through agent-os and jsonschema; demo --factory build succeeds.

findings.title: Python config and conversation models are incompatible with shipped desired configuration
findings.requirement: The agent-os CLI must validate the repository's own canonical configuration and conversation artifacts.
findings.reproduction: uv run agent-os config-validate exits 1 against .agent-os/config.yaml; uv run agent-os decision-validate .agent-os/factories/example.conversation-decision.json exits 1. The separate validators accept the same files.
findings.impact: Two incompatible contract systems exist; the repo cannot dogfood its CLI and fresh agents cannot rely on a single schema.
findings.recommendation: Unify Python and JSON Schema structures and add tests loading every canonical example/config via both validation paths.
findings.verification: agent-os config-validate and decision-validate succeed on shipped artifacts and reject shared negative fixtures.

findings.title: READY validator can approve the wrong lifecycle and underspecifies required evidence
findings.requirement: READY must be derived only from READY_REVIEW with full DoR and structured evidence.
findings.reproduction: Ticket.lifecycle is never checked by validate_definition_of_ready; a digest-bound ticket in INBOX can return ready=true if other minimal string lists are populated. Acceptance criteria have no evidence mapping; dependencies are unstructured strings and any nonempty list is treated unresolved.
findings.impact: Implementation admission can violate the architecture's core planning gate or block valid tickets with resolved dependencies.
findings.recommendation: Require READY_REVIEW, structured acceptance/evidence and dependency status, relevant product/technical owners and blocking questions; add state-specific negative tests.
findings.verification: INBOX/PLANNING cannot become ready; unresolved dependency blocks while resolved dependency does not; each criterion requires evidence.

findings.title: Run context API permits contradictory ticket and top-level base revisions
findings.requirement: A context bundle must be internally consistent and bound to one exact repository base.
findings.reproduction: create_run_context accepts base_revision separately and does not compare it with ticket.base_revision; a caller can approve and emit a bundle containing two different bases.
findings.impact: A worker or verifier can operate on a base different from the ticket record while the bundle still passes its own approval validation.
findings.recommendation: Remove the redundant argument or enforce exact equality before digesting; test mismatch rejection.
findings.verification: Context creation raises on any base mismatch.

residual_uncertainty: Additional cross-contract mismatches likely exist and are under independent review.
